extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO examiners handling continuation/divisional/CIP filings from PCT applications designating the United States
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and handling guidance for filing a U.S. national continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part (a 'bypass') of an international (PCT) application that designates the United States, and for establishing benefit/priority to the international or earlier foreign applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of filing a bypass application (continuation/divisional/CIP) of a PCT application
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. national application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) may be filed during the pendency of an international application designating the United States without entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371; such filings are commonly called 'bypass' applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis includes 35 U.S.C. 363 (effect of international application from international filing date), 371(d) (failure to timely comply with 371(c) is regarded as abandonment), and 365(c) (entitlement to benefit under 120 subject to conditions). Continuation-in-part (CIP) applications are typically used to add matter not supported by the international application because new matter may not be added to a U.S. national stage application (see 37 CFR 1.121(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a specific reference to the prior international (PCT) application
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c), the continuing U.S. application must include a specific reference to the prior international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed prior to Sept. 16, 2012 the specific reference must either be in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title or included in an application data sheet (ADS) (see 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2) and 1.78(h)). If filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, the specific reference must be contained in an ADS (37 CFR 1.78(d)(2)). The reference must identify the parent international application by international application number and international filing date and indicate the relationship of the applications (continuation, continuation-in-part, or division). The required reference must be submitted within the time period provided by 37 CFR 1.78(d)(3); that time period is not extendable. A certified copy (and English translation if necessary) of the international application may be required to perfect the benefit claim when the international application did not originate in the U.S. or when necessary (e.g., an intervening reference is found). If the international application was published under PCT Article 21, a certified copy is not normally necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copendency requirement (continuing application must be copending with the international application)
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. national application is copending with a prior international application if the international application was pending on the filing date of the U.S. national application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally an international application becomes abandoned as to the U.S. upon expiration of 30 months from the priority date (unless a proper submission under 35 U.S.C. 371 to enter the U.S. national phase is filed before that 30-month expiration). Thus a national application filed before the 30-month expiration will be copending unless the international application was withdrawn (either generally or as to the U.S.) prior to the filing of the national application. For older cases where the 20-month rule applied (20-month expiration before Apr. 1, 2002), additional rules (e.g., timely demand electing the U.S.) may apply. To determine withdrawal, the examiner may inspect the Home Copy of the international application file (if USPTO was receiving Office) or require applicant to certify non-withdrawal. Applicant should certify at filing that the international application has not been withdrawn to expedite examination. If the national application claiming benefit was filed after the 30-month period, there will be no copendency absent a timely and proper submission to enter the national phase under 35 U.S.C. 371. The existence of a national stage application may be checked via the Patent Data Portal and national stage records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common-inventor requirement (at least one inventor in common)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) the continuing application must have at least one inventor in common with the prior international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors are normally identified on the cover page of the published international application and in the PCT Gazette; examiner/applicant should verify inventorship from those sources as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) must be made in the continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) must be made in the continuing U.S. application to obtain the benefit of the filing date of the earlier foreign application, regardless of whether such a claim was made in the parent international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreign priority claim is proper if the continuing application or the parent international application was filed not later than 12 months after the filing date of the foreign application (37 CFR 1.55(b)). It is also proper if filed after 12 months but within two months from such expiration if the right of priority is restored under 37 CFR 1.55(c). The required claim must be made within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.55(d)(1); that time period is not extendable. A certified copy of any foreign priority document must be provided unless the requirements of 37 CFR 1.55(h) or (i) are met or the parent international application has entered the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 and the national stage application contains the priority document. If the latter is true, the continuing application may state that the priority document is contained in the national stage application. See MPEP § 214.01 and MPEP § 1893.03(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate international application benefit claims must include specific reference to earlier application
rubrics_metrics.description: If benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and/or under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) is being claimed to an earlier filed national application via an intermediate international application, the intermediate international application must contain a specific reference to the earlier application as required by 37 CFR 1.78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific reference will usually appear on the cover page of the published international application and/or in the first sentence(s) of the description of the published application. Lack of a proper reference in the published international application does not necessarily mean the reference was not contained in the intermediate international application (it may have been filed in a separate paper after publication or a petition to accept a late benefit claim may be present). Examiners may need to inspect the international application file (if USPTO was receiving Office) to determine whether 37 CFR 1.78 requirements were satisfied after publication. Examiner may contact International Patent Legal Administration for assistance. See MPEP § 211.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy and translation requirements for priority and international application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy (and an English translation if necessary) of the international application or foreign priority documents may be required to perfect claims for benefit/priority in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certified copy is often required when the international application did not originate in the U.S. and when necessary to assess intervening references or claim priority. If the international application was published by the International Bureau under PCT Article 21, a certified copy would not normally be necessary. For foreign priority documents, a certified copy is required unless the exceptions in 37 CFR 1.55(h) or (i) are satisfied or the priority document is contained in the national stage application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules and non-extendability of required submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Various required submissions and deadlines (e.g., the specific reference under 37 CFR 1.78(d)(3) and foreign priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55(d)(1)) are subject to strict time periods that are not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure required references and priority claims are timely submitted in the correct form (ADS, specification placement, certified copies) because the statutory/regulatory time periods for these requirements are non-extendable. Examiners should verify whether filings meet these deadline requirements and may require supporting proof when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for older PCT cases where 20-month demand rules applied
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications subject to the older 20‑month demand regime (where the 20‑month period from the priority date expired before April 1, 2002), additional proof may be required to establish entitlement to benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a demand electing the United States prior to expiration of 19 months from the priority date was necessary to extend the international phase to 30 months and such demand was not timely filed, the international application may have become abandoned at 20 months unless a proper submission under 35 U.S.C. 371 was made. Applicants may be required to submit proof of filing of the demand (e.g., Notification of Receipt of Demand by Competent IPEA — Form PCT/IPEA/402 and Notification Concerning Elected Offices Notified of Their Election — Form PCT/IB/332) showing the demand/election were timely made. See related discussion in MPEP § 1893.01(a)(1).
